anya: Heads up, onboarding OrbitonX (converted from vendor checkpoint). Getting odd generation drift vs reference — seems tied to rotary scaling + vocab mapping. minimal repro below.

miguel: ack — can you paste the conversion command + a short diff of token ids?

anya: conversion command: `python tools/convert_checkpoint.py --src orbitonx.ckpt --dst redwood/orbitonx.pt --vocab src_vocab.json --tgt-vocab tgt_vocab.json`
Log snippet: ```INFO: mapped 50200 tokens, 15 tokens unmapped
WARN: token-id offset detected: +2 for bytepair range 200-999```

sam: +2 offset sounds bad. Is that only in the vocab or also in kv-cache lookups?

anya: quick check: running a 512-step gen with reference (vendor) vs converted: vendor top-1 match 92%, converted 72%. When I zero rotary scaling (set rotary_scale=1.0) match jumps to 89%.

lee: so rotary scaling normalization differs. OrbitonX uses headwise rotary freq multiplier (per-head freq). Our converter currently assumes global scale. That'd explain the short-term divergence.

anya: verified — applying per-head multiplier from src metadata (freq_factors = [1.0, 0.98, ...]) -> reduces immediate token mismatch to 90%. But long-context (1024) hallucination spikes.

miguel: maybe kv-cache indexing misaligned because of that +2 token offset. If token IDs used for prefix cache keys are shifted, long contexts will read wrong cached keys. Can you print first 10 kv-keys hashes for both models for the same prompt?

anya: did that. sample hashes (first 3):
vendor: ["h1:0x9a...","h2:0x3f...","h3:0x7b..."]
converted: ["h1:0x9a...","h2:0x3f...","h3:0x7b..."]
they match for initial tokens, mismatch starts at token id 205 -> vendor uses id 205, converted uses 207.

sam: so two independent issues: token-id mapping gap and rotary per-head scale. Both interact in long-context regressions. Which is higher priority? Fixing kv-id mapping seems like it would recover cache behavior.

anya: agreed. quick patch in converter to collapse unmapped tokens into nearest bpe-id (instead of shifting ranges) fixes the +2 offset and improves long-context perplexity by ~12%. But we still see a soft-quality delta.

lee: that remaining delta likely from fp16->int4 quant path — did you run the INT4 path?

anya: yes. INT4 quantized model shows worse top-1 match (converted INT4 60% vs converted fp16 88%). But if I apply per-head rotary scaling tweak + bias-correction during quant, INT4 match moves to 75%.

miguel: what's the quant toolchain? `quantize_nbits.py` with blockwise per-channel? Any asymmetric stats?

anya: pipeline: `python tools/quantize_nbits.py --model redwood/orbitonx.pt --bits 4 --method blockwise --clip 0.995`
Observations: attention proj weights have heavy tail; per-channel clipping helps but we need bias-correction for rotary proj.

ci-bot: CI: regen-evals started for orbitonx/converted on perf-worker-7 (job 8842).

eval-bot: Quick eval snapshot: lm-perplexity (512): vendor fp16 18.2, converted fp16 19.1, converted INT4 23.5, converted INT4 +rotary-bias-correct 20.6. (short prompt set)

sam: good to have numbers. Action items?

anya: 1) finalize converter fix to avoid id-range shifts (PR ready, tests failing on a couple edge cases). 2) add per-head rotary import in conversion metadata (PR in progress). 3) enhance INT4 quant pipeline to run rotary bias-correction & per-channel clip sweeps.

lee: also add a small token-level smoke test: for a deterministic short prompt, compare first 64 logits between vendor and converted (fp16) and assert cosine(logits) > 0.995. That will catch mapping/rotary regressions earlier.

miguel: +1 on smoke test. I'll help with unit test harness and a tiny fixture.

anya: thanks — I'll post PR links in this thread when ready. For context, reproducible snippet to run locally:```python
from rdl.tools import load_model
m = load_model('redwood/orbitonx.pt')
prompt = 'In the beginning' # deterministic small set
out = m.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=64)
print(out)
```

sam: if PRs land, let's schedule a canary run on dedicated pool before default catalog entry. Need to avoid breaking hosted customers. :eyes:

anya: agreed. will coordinate canary once fixes merged. Thanks all. :pray:
